Hi Marcus — quick answers on billing/token and endpoint details so you can plan integration.

Token accounting (short):
- We count tokens per request payload. If you batch 1200 candidates into a single request, tokens are measured on the full request (prompt + candidates + system messages). So batching reduces per-candidate overhead dramatically, but peak token rate is what we enforce for rate limits.
- Example: if each candidate adds ~40 tokens and you have a 256-token explanation per returned item for top-N, a single 1200-candidate request could approach ~60k tokens depending on response shaping. Please use traffic_estimates.xlsx to model the exact scenarios.

Endpoints & headers:
- Primary generation endpoint (Hosted): POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
- Query params: ?model=rw-large-qa&stream=true (streaming enabled to start returning top scorers quickly)
- Required headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> ; X-Client-Env: staging|prod ; X-Request-ID: <uuid>
- Rate limits (pilot default): 500 requests/min per key, token cap 10,000 tokens/min; burst soft cap 1,800 requests/min for up to 30s. We can raise these for pilot if you provide 1-week traffic profile.

SLOs & operational controls:
- We will enable prefix KV caching (if candidates share prefixes) and recommend you use streaming to avoid waiting for full batch decode. That reduces median latency.
- We can set up canary routing to route 5% of prod traffic to Hosted endpoint initially.

Next actions:
1) Lukas: provision per-environment endpoints and create two API keys (staging/prod) with default pilot quotas.
2) Marcus: populate traffic_estimates.xlsx with 3 typical workloads (low/median/peak) and share by EOD Tue.
3) We'll schedule a 45m integration call after keys are created — propose Wed 8/6 10:00 PT.
